codeReview.summary: The feature adds substantial bench functionality and tests, but there is a blocking correctness flaw in TPS computation that makes per-metric benchmark reporting/comparison unreliable.

issues.description: Prompt/gen TPS are mathematically forced to the same value: `prompt_tps` and `gen_tps` are computed by dividing token counts by proportional slices of the same `total_time` (`prompt_fraction`/`gen_fraction`), which simplifies both metrics to `total_tokens / total_time`. This breaks the required per-metric benchmark reporting and PASS/WARN/FAIL comparison behavior.

CLI always prints "✓ Results saved" when `--save` is passed, but core persistence is conditional (`src/mlx_stack/core/benchmark.py:1143` only saves when a hardware profile is available). In profile-detection failure paths, users can be told results were saved even though no file was written.

`pull --bench` now calls full `run_benchmark()` (3 iterations of 1024+100 and optional tool-calling), while command/help text still describe a "quick benchmark". This risks runtime regression against the quick-benchmark expectation in VAL-CROSS-014.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission feature metadata points workers to `cli-feature`, but that skill was not invokable in the worker environment, and the implementation then diverged from the skill's tests-first procedure.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: features.json for `bench-command` sets `skillName` to `cli-feature`; transcript skeleton shows `Error: Skill "cli-feature" not found` and then code creation (`core/benchmark.py`, `cli/bench.py`) before test creation; `.factory/skills/cli-feature/SKILL.md` explicitly requires Step 2/3 tests-first workflow.

summary: Reviewed handoff, diff, transcript skeleton, and shared-state artifacts for `bench-command`. Result: fail due to a blocking TPS-computation bug that invalidates per-metric benchmark comparison; additional non-blocking UX/regression risks were noted.
